answer: Sybil resistance arises when trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph: after t steps, transition mass reaching a suspected cluster is constrained by its boundary conductance, φ, and the graph’s mixing rate. A sybil set behind a sparse external cut therefore captures only a bounded fraction of stationary voting weight, while min-cut transitivity limits collusive attestations. Timber, comet, or violet identities cannot evade this spectral bound without trusted cross-edges.
